moves.words: Horn defines change as potency reduced to act and identifies God as necessary, unlimited, and perfectly good.

Principal limitation: The definition does not itself establish that observed change terminates in one unlimited personal source rather than a thinner metaphysical ground, leaving the comparative inference materially less secure than the confident conclusion requires. strengths: Defines the classical divine target and core metaphysical vocabulary with unusual clarity.
Keeps contingency, temporal beginning, fine-tuning, morality, and convergence as distinguishable argumentative routes.
Answers several objections directly, especially the infinity distinction and evidential status of moral perception.

blunders.text: Treats conceivable morally sufficient reasons as an incomplete answer to a comparative hiddenness likelihood challenge.
Moves from multiple partial conclusions toward one classical deity without fully establishing identity or evidential independence.

strengths: Maintains the proper agnostic burden without claiming to prove that no deity exists.
Repeatedly demands explicit comparison among theism, naturalism, and developed rival supernatural explanations.
Frames suffering and nonresistant nonbelief as probabilistic evidence with careful conditional qualifications.

blunders.text: Invokes several rival possibilities without developing their priors, mechanisms, or independent explanatory virtues.
Presses uncertainty effectively but sometimes leaves his own comparative likelihood judgments less supported than his standard requires.

finalArgument.thesis: The convergent evidence is best explained by one necessary, intelligent, and perfectly good source.
premises: Contingent reality supplies evidence for a nonderivative ground rather than an unexplained regress of derivative conditions.
A genuine cosmic beginning would add evidence for causation that is not itself located within physical time.
Life-permitting order is more expected if fundamental reality includes purposive intelligence than under an unspecified brute foundation.
Objective moral authority is more intelligible if value belongs necessarily to the character of ultimate reality.
When partly independent clues converge on compatible attributes, their joint support can exceed each argument’s isolated force.
finalArgument.conclusion: Therefore, if these comparisons survive their live burdens, classical theism gains cumulative support beyond any single demonstration.

newArguments.title: Cross-route identity test
newArguments.text: Convergence strengthens theism only if the necessary ground, temporal cause, designer, and moral foundation are independently shown to be one reality. Identity can be tested by asking whether each route entails compatible modal properties, explanatory roles, and uniqueness conditions, rather than simply assigning every favorable conclusion the same name.

newArguments.title: Specified divine expectations
newArguments.text: Theism becomes more discriminating when it states which combinations of order, moral awareness, hiddenness, and suffering are probable given particular divine purposes. A constrained account can risk evidential failure, but it also answers the objection that an unlimited divine will accommodates every possible observation equally well.

finalArgument.thesis: Agnosticism remains warranted when theistic arguments leave their key likelihood comparisons and rival explanations unresolved.
premises: Valid form cannot compensate for premises whose modal, scientific, or moral support remains substantially disputed.
A supernatural cause does not uniquely identify one God, perfect goodness, classical simplicity, or providential governance.
Severe suffering and sincere nonresistant nonbelief appear less expected under some ordinary formulations of perfect love.
Merely conceivable divine reasons establish compatibility but do not determine comparative probability or explain the observed distribution.
Rival hypotheses matter when they expose underdetermination even before any one rival becomes independently probable.
finalArgument.conclusion: Therefore confidence in classical theism should be withheld until its predictions and comparative advantages are stated and defended more precisely.

newArguments.title: Disclosure calibration
newArguments.text: A loving deity could calibrate evidence to individual resistance: clearer disclosure for sincere seekers need not coerce action, because knowledge of another person never guarantees trust or obedience. Persistent nonresistant nonbelief therefore requires a more specific relational explanation than the general claim that ambiguity preserves freedom.

newArguments.title: Rival development threshold
newArguments.text: Bare logical alternatives prevent entailment but do not automatically defeat an inference to the best explanation. The agnostic critique becomes stronger when at least one rival specifies a mechanism, prior rationale, and contrasting predictions, allowing underdetermination to be measured rather than asserted through an indefinitely expandable list of possibilities.
